world: Old rural Norway, in a scattered farming parish of grey log farms with turf roofs among fields, spruce forest and bogs. The widower's small farm has a low log house with a stone chimney and a field of tall, ripe hemp below it. Beyond the farms lies a great, dark spruce forest. The farms that Giske and the thieves raid have a sheep shed built wall to wall with the farmer's sleeping room, a goose house of grey logs and, at the rich farmer's at the forest edge, a stabbur: a dark timber storehouse on posts with a steep little stair, hung inside with hams and sausages above shelves of round pea bread. The turnip patch is a clearing in the woods on a slope, with old stumps and rows of purple turnips, above a soft brown bog of tussocks and stumps.
palette: August, between haymaking and harvest: a hot, hazy afternoon over the green-gold hemp; then three moonlit nights in deep indigo and blue-black, with a thin sickle moon, cold starlight and the small yellow glow of a lantern or candle; and a pearl-grey Sunday dawn with low mist over the brown bog and dew on purple turnips. Accents: greasy soot black, plum purple and turnip violet.

cast.look: A very tall, strong housekeeper of about thirty, a head taller than any man, with extremely long legs and big bare feet. She has a long oval face, a wide eager smile, a small turned-up nose, bright hazel eyes and flaxen hair wound into a tall bun. Her plum-purple homespun dress is hacked off raggedly at the knees, and her arms and legs are smeared greasy black with tallow and soot like a chimney sweep's, with sooty smudges on her face. A ring of iron keys hangs at her belt.
cast.portrait: Background: the tall hemp field in hazy afternoon light.

simplified.name: Giske
simplified.description: Husholderska som blir smurt inn med talg og sot, tror hun er fanden, og blir både ivrig hjelper og katastrofe for to tyver på nattetokt.

english.name: Giske
english.description: A vain, talkative housekeeper who is smeared with tallow and pipe-soot, mistakes herself for the Devil, and blunders loudly through a string of thefts and panicked encounters.

cast.look: A skinny, stooped widower of about fifty with a long, narrow, tired face, heavy-lidded eyes, a long crooked nose, hollow cheeks, a scruffy salt-and-pepper chin beard and thin dark hair combed flat. He wears a collarless undyed linen shirt, dark-blue braces, baggy grey homespun breeches, a darned heather-brown knitted wool jacket and worn wooden-soled shoes, and always has a short, curved pipe in the corner of his mouth.
cast.portrait: Background: his low farmhouse room with a stone hearth.

simplified.name: Enkemannen
simplified.description: Mannen hun arbeider hos, som vil bli kvitt Giske og lager spøken som får henne til å tro hun er fanden.

english.name: The Widower
english.description: Giske’s master, a weary widower who devises the cruel prank to rid himself of her constant demands to marry.

cast.look: A skinny, jittery thief of about thirty, a head shorter than Giske, with a long pale face, a long pointy nose, big frightened eyes, a wispy ginger goatee and lank hair under a floppy black knitted stocking cap. He wears a patched charcoal wool jacket too short in the arms, grey striped breeches, grey stockings and shoes wrapped in rags, and carries an empty sack under his arm.
cast.portrait: Background: the dark spruce forest at dusk.

simplified.name: Den tynne tyven
simplified.description: Den ene av de to sultne tyvene som tar Giske med på nattetokt fordi hun er så godt kjent på gårdene. Han er tynn og skvetten og hysjer mest av alle.

english.name: The Skinny Thief
english.description: One of the two hungry thieves who take Giske along on their night raids because she knows the farms so well. He is thin and jumpy, and does most of the hushing.

cast.look: A short, round, nervous thief of about forty, much shorter than Giske, with a round red face, puffy cheeks, a stubbly double chin, tiny eyes, a big bushy black moustache and a bald head under a greasy brown wool cap. He wears a tight mustard-brown waistcoat with one button missing over a grey shirt, baggy brown trousers held up with a rope and big clumsy boots, and carries a coil of rope over his shoulder.
cast.portrait: Background: the dark spruce forest at dusk.

simplified.name: Den tykke tyven
simplified.description: Den andre av de to tyvene. Han er liten og rund, sulten som en ulv og livredd for å bli tatt.

english.name: The Plump Thief
english.description: The other of the two thieves: short, round, hungry as a wolf and terrified of being caught.

cast.look: A lean, wiry farmer of about forty-five with a bony, hollow-cheeked face, a hooked nose, bristly grey stubble, startled round eyes and wild, tousled grey hair, just woken from sleep. He wears only a long, loose, undyed linen nightshirt that reaches his knees, with bare skinny legs and bare feet, and holds up a small tin lantern with a candle burning inside.
cast.portrait: Background: his farmyard and sheep shed at night.

simplified.name: Bonden
simplified.description: Bonden som våkner av skrålet i sauehuset, blir slått over ende av noe stort og svart, og setter seg til å lese og be.

english.name: The Farmer
english.description: The farmer who is woken by the racket in his sheep shed, is bowled over by something big and black, and sits down to read the Bible and pray.

cast.look: A short, sturdy, bow-legged farmer of about fifty, one of the richest in the parish, with a square, weather-beaten face, a big bristly chestnut moustache, round startled eyes, bushy eyebrows and wiry grey hair sticking up under a wide, frayed straw hat. He wears a rust-orange wool waistcoat with silver buttons over a white linen shirt, green knee breeches pulled on in a hurry, long grey stockings and wooden clogs.
cast.portrait: Background: the turnip patch in the morning mist.

simplified.name: Bonden med nepebråten
simplified.description: En av de rikeste bøndene i bygda. Han ser fanden i nepeåkeren sin, lokker presten ut med en feit kalvestek og bærer ham over myra på ryggen.

english.name: The Turnip Farmer
english.description: One of the richest farmers in the parish. He sees the Devil in his turnip patch, tempts the priest out with a fat roast of veal and carries him across the bog on his back.

cast.look: A very round, heavy priest of about sixty-five with a big belly, short legs, a pink, jowly, clean-shaven face, puffy sleepy eyes, bushy white eyebrows and a fringe of white curls under a long red-and-white striped nightcap with a tassel. He wears a crumpled white nightshirt stuffed into black trousers he has dragged on in a hurry, with the braces dangling, and a pair of blue felt slippers.
cast.portrait: Background: the dim parlour of the parsonage.

simplified.name: Presten
simplified.description: Blir hentet for å «binde fanden», men ender hjelpeløs da bonden flykter i panikk.

english.name: The Priest
english.description: A local priest hurried out on Sunday morning in slippers and nightcap to bind the supposed Devil, only to be tossed into a sucking bog in the confusion.

cover.prompt: A forest path at night under a big, pale moon, with dark spruces on both sides. Giske strides ahead on her long black legs, grinning, pointing eagerly towards a dark farm far off between the trees and clearly about to say something loud. Close behind her creep the Skinny Thief, clutching his empty sack, and the Plump Thief, with his coil of rope, both pressing a finger to their lips and glancing around in panic.

simplified.caption: Giske tror hun er fanden selv, og hun vil så gjerne hjelpe til.
simplified.alt: Giske går foran på en skogssti i måneskinnet med svarte armer og bein og peker ivrig. Bak henne lister to tyver seg fram og holder fingeren foran munnen.

english.caption: Giske believes she is the Devil himself, and she is ever so eager to help.
english.alt: Giske strides along a moonlit forest path with black arms and legs, pointing eagerly. Behind her, two thieves creep along with their fingers to their lips.

illustrations.prompt: At the edge of a field of tall, ripe hemp on a hazy afternoon, Giske lies fast asleep on her back among bundles of pulled hemp, snoring with her mouth open and her long legs stretched out. The Widower kneels beside her, pipe between his teeth and a small pot of greasy black soot in one hand, smearing the last streaks onto her arm with a grim, weary face. A big pair of iron shears and a long cut-off strip of plum-purple skirt lie in the stubble beside them.

simplified.anchor: Mens hun sov, kom mannen med ei saks og klipte det lange skjørtet hennes av ved knærne. Så
simplified.caption: Mens Giske sov, smurte mannen henne inn med talg og sot.
simplified.alt: Giske sover i hampåkeren med svarte bein og skjørtet klipt av ved knærne. Enkemannen sitter på kne ved siden av henne og smører sot på armen hennes. I gresset ligger ei stor saks.

english.anchor: While she slept, the man came along with a pair of shears and cut her long skirt off at the knees.
english.caption: While she slept, the man smeared her with tallow and soot.
english.alt: Giske lies asleep in the hemp field with blackened legs and her skirt cut off at the knees. The widower kneels beside her, smearing soot on her arm. A big pair of shears lies in the grass.

illustrations.prompt: Inside a low farmhouse room in the late afternoon, the door has just swung open, and Giske stoops in the doorway with her head bent under the lintel, black-armed and black-legged in her hacked-off skirt, asking her question with a puzzled, earnest frown. The Widower sits at the plank table beside a tall ticking clock, pipe in hand, and answers her with a perfectly straight face, as if she were a stranger.

simplified.anchor: Men hun ville vite sikkert hvordan det hang sammen.
simplified.caption: «Er Giske hjemme i dag?»
simplified.alt: Giske, svart på armer og bein, bøyer seg inn gjennom døra og spør. Enkemannen sitter ved bordet med pipa og svarer uten å fortrekke en mine.

english.anchor: But she wanted to be sure.
english.caption: “Is Giske at home today?”
english.alt: Giske, black-armed and black-legged, stoops in the doorway to ask her question. The widower sits at the table with his pipe and answers with a perfectly straight face.

illustrations.prompt: A great, dark spruce forest at dusk. The Skinny Thief and the Plump Thief run for their lives down a mossy path, arms flailing, looking back over their shoulders in terror, the Plump Thief's cap flying off his bald head. Right on their heels comes Giske with enormous long-legged strides, her black arms held out, calling after them with a friendly, eager face. Low red light slants between the tree trunks.

simplified.caption: Tyvene trodde den onde selv var ute etter dem.
simplified.alt: To tyver løper for livet gjennom en mørk granskog. Rett bak dem kommer Giske med lange steg og svarte armer og bein.

english.anchor: The thieves didn’t see it that way.
english.caption: The thieves thought the Evil One had come to fetch them.
english.alt: Two thieves run for their lives through a dark spruce forest. Right behind them comes Giske, with long strides and black arms and legs.

illustrations.prompt: Inside a dark sheep shed at night, lit by a shaft of moonlight from the open door, Giske stands among seven startled woolly sheep and a horned ram, her long black arms flung wide and her head thrown back, shouting at the top of her voice. In the low doorway, the Skinny Thief and the Plump Thief crouch with their fingers pressed to their lips, eyes bulging with horror.

simplified.anchor: «Vil dere ha bukk eller søye? Her er nok å ta av!»
simplified.caption: «Vil dere ha bukk eller søye? Her er nok å ta av!»
simplified.alt: Inne i et mørkt sauehus står Giske blant sauene med armene ut og roper. I døråpningen holder tyvene fingeren foran munnen.

english.anchor: “Do you want a ram or a ewe? There’s plenty to take!”
english.caption: “Do you want a ram or a ewe? There’s plenty to take!”
english.alt: Inside a dark sheep shed, Giske stands among the sheep with her arms flung wide, shouting. In the doorway the thieves press their fingers to their lips.

illustrations.prompt: A farmyard at night under a thin moon. The Sheep Farmer has just been bowled clean over and lies flat on his back in the yard, holding his lantern up in one hand, his mouth wide open in shock. Giske races on past him with huge strides after the Skinny Thief and the Plump Thief, who are scrambling over the rail fence at the edge of the yard. Behind them the door of the sheep shed stands open, with three sheep peering out.

simplified.anchor: Imens hadde bonden våknet av alt skrålet, og nå kom han ut i bare skjorta for å se hva som sto på.
simplified.caption: Giske satte etter tyvene så fort at hun løp bonden over ende.
simplified.alt: Om natta ligger bonden på ryggen på gårdsplassen i bare skjorta, med lykta i hånda. Giske løper forbi etter tyvene, som klatrer over gjerdet.

english.anchor: By now all the racket had woken the farmer on the other side of the wall.
english.caption: Giske tore after the thieves so fast that she bowled the farmer clean over.
english.alt: At night the farmer lies flat on his back in the yard in his nightshirt, holding up his lantern. Giske races past after the thieves, who are scrambling over the fence.

illustrations.prompt: Night outside a grey log goose house. Out of its open door burst nine white geese, all shrieking at once with their necks stretched out and their wings flapping. The Skinny Thief and the Plump Thief are already bolting across the yard, and Giske leaps after them on her long bare black legs, her hacked-off skirt flying above her knees. In the doorway of the farmhouse, a stout, bald farmer in a white nightshirt holds up a candle and stares at her, frozen with terror.

simplified.anchor: Mens de sto og kranglet om dette, begynte en av gjessene å skrike.
simplified.caption: Bonden trodde det var den svarte fanden selv.
simplified.alt: Gjessene skriker og flakser ut av gåsehuset. Tyvene springer over gårdsplassen med Giske etter seg, mens en bonde i nattskjorte står i døra med et lys og stirrer.

english.anchor: While they stood there bickering, one of the geese began to shriek.
english.caption: The farmer took her for the black Devil himself.
english.alt: The geese shriek and flap out of the goose house. The thieves dash across the yard with Giske after them, while a farmer in a nightshirt stands in his doorway with a candle, staring.

illustrations.prompt: Night at a rich farm at the edge of the forest. Giske stands in the open door at the top of the steep little stair of a dark timber storehouse on posts; behind her, in the moonlight, hams and sausages hang in rows from the rafters above shelves of round pea bread. Her eyes shine with delight and she is drawing an enormous breath to shout. At the foot of the stair, the Skinny Thief and the Plump Thief hiss up at her, flapping their hands for quiet.

simplified.anchor: Der inne var det fullt av god mat: kjøtt og flesk og pølser og ertebrød. Tyvene hysjet
simplified.caption: Der inne var det fullt av god mat.
simplified.alt: Giske står i døra til et stabbur fullt av skinker, pølser og brød og trekker pusten for å rope. Nede ved trappa hysjer tyvene på henne.

english.anchor: Inside it was packed with every good thing: meat and bacon and sausages and pea bread.
english.caption: Inside it was packed with every good thing.
english.alt: Giske stands in the door of a storehouse full of hams, sausages and bread, taking a deep breath to shout. At the foot of the steps the thieves hush her.

illustrations.prompt: A wide view over the parish at midnight under a sickle moon: dark log farms scattered over the hillsides, and on every farm a small window glowing with candlelight. In the nearest farmhouse, seen through its window, a farmer in a nightshirt reads aloud from a big old Bible held up in both hands, its dark leather cover towards us, while his wife, three children and two farmhands kneel around the table with their hands folded and their eyes squeezed shut.

simplified.anchor: Da bonden fikk se det stygge beistet, trodde han også at fanden var løs
simplified.caption: Så from hadde bygda ikke vært på mange år.
simplified.alt: Over hele bygda lyser det i vinduene midt på natta. I den nærmeste stua leser bonden høyt av Bibelen, mens familien kneler rundt bordet og ber.

english.anchor: When the farmer saw that ugly beast, he too believed the Devil was loose
english.caption: The parish hadn’t been so devout in years.
english.alt: Candlelight glows in windows all over the parish in the middle of the night. In the nearest farmhouse, the farmer reads aloud from the Bible while his family kneel around the table and pray.

illustrations.prompt: Early on a misty Sunday morning, the Turnip Farmer stands at the edge of a soft brown bog, seen from the side, frozen with fright, his hair standing on end under his straw hat. Far up the slope, in a clearing among the spruces, Giske crouches among the rows of turnips, a tall black shape half hidden in the pearl-grey mist, tugging and tugging at them.

simplified.anchor: Bonden som eide nepeåkeren, hadde ikke fått sove for alt snakket om fanden,
simplified.caption: Han fikk se noe svart oppe i åkeren som rusket og rusket.
simplified.alt: En søndag morgen står bonden ved myra og stirrer skrekkslagen opp mot nepeåkeren. Der oppe i tåka rusker en høy, svart skikkelse i nepene.

english.anchor: The farmer who owned the turnip patch had hardly slept for all the talk of the Devil
english.caption: He saw something black up among the turnips, tugging and tugging.
english.alt: Early on a Sunday morning, the farmer stands by the bog, staring up at the turnip patch in terror. Up in the mist, a tall black figure is tugging at the turnips.

illustrations.prompt: In the dim parlour of the parsonage in grey morning light, the Priest comes hurrying down a steep wooden staircase in his nightcap and slippers, hopping on one foot as he drags his trousers up, his face bright at the thought of a fat roast of veal. The Turnip Farmer waits on a rag rug with his straw hat crushed in his hands. At the foot of the stairs stands a young maid in a white apron.

simplified.anchor: Han la i vei til prestegården.
simplified.caption: Presten rev på seg buksene og kom ned i tøfler og nattlue.
simplified.alt: Presten skynder seg ned trappa i nattlue og tøfler og drar på seg buksene. Bonden venter i stua med hatten i hendene, og ved trappa står jenta.

english.anchor: He set off for the parsonage.
english.caption: The priest dragged on his trousers and came straight down in his slippers and nightcap.
english.alt: The priest hurries down the stairs in his nightcap and slippers, dragging on his trousers. The farmer waits in the parlour with his hat in his hands, and the maid stands by the stairs.

illustrations.prompt: A wide view of the brown bog below the turnip patch on a misty Sunday morning. In the middle of the bog, the Priest sits stuck up to his waist in brown mud among the tussocks, his nightcap askew, open-mouthed with outrage. The Turnip Farmer runs off across the tussocks for his life, straw hat flying. Far up the slope, at the edge of the turnip clearing, Giske stands with a turnip in each hand, staring after him in bewilderment.

simplified.anchor: Og så ble han så redd at han slengte presten midt ut i myra og la på sprang.
simplified.caption: Og er ikke presten kommet opp, så ligger han der nok ennå.
simplified.alt: Presten sitter fast i gjørma midt ute på myra med nattlua på snei. Bonden springer for livet over tuene, og oppe i nepeåkeren står Giske og ser etter ham.

english.anchor: And he was so frightened that he flung the priest into the middle of the bog and ran for his life.
english.caption: And if the priest hasn’t got out, he’s lying there still.
english.alt: The priest is stuck in the mud in the middle of the bog, his nightcap askew. The farmer runs for his life across the tussocks, and up at the turnip patch Giske stares after him.
